issue.title: Drop a statement onto the upload form
issue.body:
Most of our statements arrive as email attachments. Today I save each one, click
"Choose a CSV file", find it again in the folder and upload it. Could the upload
form accept a file dragged onto it from the desktop or from the mail app?
Picking one file at a time is fine; it's the file dialog every time that slows
us down at month end.

input.title: Accept a CSV file dragged onto the upload form
input.body:
File: src/components/UploadForm.tsx

The form's only way to pick a file is the hidden file input inside the "Choose a CSV file" label. Add drag-and-drop to the form element: handle dragover (preventDefault so the drop is allowed, and show a highlight class), dragleave to clear it, and drop to take the first dropped file, checking it is a .csv or text/csv, then set it with setFile. Keep the single-file behaviour the reporter described and leave the submit path unchanged.

The upload form only accepts a file through its file-picker input, with no drag-and-drop handling. Dropping a file on it today makes the browser open the CSV instead, and the console shows `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'files')`. A draft pull request (pr-25) proposes adding drop handlers to the form in this component, so a CSV dragged from the desktop or a mail app is taken as the one file to upload.

Thanks for the detailed report; here is what triage found.

The upload form only accepts a file through its file-picker input, with no drag-and-drop handling. Dropping a file on it today makes the browser open the CSV instead, and the console shows `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'files')`. A draft pull request (pr-25) proposes adding drop handlers to the form in this component, so a CSV dragged from the desktop or a mail app is taken as the one file to upload.

In short: the upload form only accepts a file through its file-picker input, with no drag-and-drop handling.

This triage rests on the issue as it was filed and on what RepoMind's own reads of the repository returned. If any of it looks wrong, a maintainer can change the label or close the draft pull request. Nothing has been merged.
